title: अंश ५ · अध्याय १९

items.text:
एवमन्तर्जले विष्णुमभिष्टूय स यादवः ।
अर्ज्जयामास सर्व्वेशं पुष्पैर्धूपैर्मनोरमैः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
evamantarjale viṣṇumabhiṣṭūya sa yādavaḥ |
arjjayāmāsa sarvveśaṃ puṣpairdhūpairmanoramaiḥ || 1 ||

items.text:
परित्यक्तान्यविषयो मनस्तत्र निवेश्य सः ।
ब्रह्मभूते चिरं स्थित्वा विरराम समाधितः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
parityaktānyaviṣayo manastatra niveśya saḥ |
brahmabhūte ciraṃ sthitvā virarāma samādhitaḥ || 2 ||

items.text:
कृतकृत्यमिवात्मानं मन्यमानो महामतिः ।
आजगाम रथं भूयो निगम्य यमुनाम्भसः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
kṛtakṛtyamivātmānaṃ manyamāno mahāmatiḥ |
ājagāma rathaṃ bhūyo nigamya yamunāmbhasaḥ || 3 ||

items.text:
राम-कृष्णौ च ददृशे यथापूर्व्वं रथे स्थितौ ।
विस्मिताक्षस्तदाक्रू रस्तञ्च कृष्णोऽभ्यभाषत ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
rāma-kṛṣṇau ca dadṛśe yathāpūrvvaṃ rathe sthitau |
vismitākṣastadākrū rastañca kṛṣṇo'bhyabhāṣata || 4 ||

items.text:
नूनं ते दृष्टमाश्वर्य्यमक्रूर!यमुनाजले ।
विस्मयोतूफूल्लनयनो भवान् संलक्ष्यते यतः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
nūnaṃ te dṛṣṭamāśvaryyamakrūra!yamunājale |
vismayotūphūllanayano bhavān saṃlakṣyate yataḥ || 5 ||

items.text:
अन्तर्जले यदाश्वर्य्यं दृष्टं तत्र मयाच्युत!
तदत्रापि हि पश्यामि मूत्तिंमत् पुरतः स्थितम् ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
antarjale yadāśvaryyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tatra mayācyuta!
tadatrāpi hi paśyāmi mūttiṃmat purataḥ sthitam || 6 ||

items.text:
जगदेतन्महाश्वर्य्य रूपं यस्य महात्मनः ।
तेनाश्वर्य्यवरेणाहं भवता कृष्ण!सङ्गतः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
jagadetanmahāśvaryya rūpaṃ yasya mahātmanaḥ |
tenāśvaryyavareṇāhaṃ bhavatā kṛṣṇa!saṅgataḥ || 7 ||

items.text:
तत् किमेतेन मथुरां व्रजामो मधुसूदन!
बिभेमि कंसाद्धिग् जन्म परपिण्डोपजीविनाम् ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
tat kimetena mathurāṃ vrajāmo madhusūdana!
bibhemi kaṃsāddhig janma parapiṇḍopajīvinām || 8 ||

items.text:
इत्युक्त्वा चोदयामास तान् हयान् वातरंहसः ।
सम्प्राप्तश्वातिसायाह्र सोऽक्रूरो मथुरां पुरीम्‌ ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
ityuktvā codayāmāsa tān hayān vātaraṃhasaḥ |
samprāptaśvātisāyāhra so'krūro mathurāṃ purīm || 9 ||

items.text:
विलोक्य मथुरां कृष्णं रामञ्चाह स यादवः ।
पद्भयां यातं महावीर्य्यो रथेनैको विशाम्यहम् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
vilokya mathurāṃ kṛṣṇaṃ rāmañcāha sa yādavaḥ |
padbhayāṃ yātaṃ mahāvīryyo rathenaiko viśāmyaham || 10 ||

items.text:
गन्तव्यं वसुदेवस्य भवद्भयां न तथा गृहम् ।
युवयोर्हि कृते वृद्धः स कंसेन निरस्यते ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
gantavyaṃ vasudevasya bhavadbhayāṃ na tathā gṛham |
yuvayorhi kṛte vṛddhaḥ sa kaṃsena nirasyate || 11 ||

items.text:
इत्युत्तवा प्रविवेशाथ सोऽकूरो मथुरां पुरीम् ।
प्रिवष्टौ रामकृष्णौ, च राजमार्गमुपागतौ ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
ityuttavā praviveśātha so'kūro mathurāṃ purīm |
privaṣṭau rāmakṛṣṇau, ca rājamārgamupāgatau || 12 ||

items.text:
स्त्रीभिर्नरैश्व सानन्दं लोचनैरभिवीक्षितौ ।
जग्मतुलीलया वीरौ दृफ्तौ बालगजाविव ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
strībhirnaraiśva sānandaṃ locanairabhivīkṣitau |
jagmatulīlayā vīrau dṛphtau bālagajāviva || 13 ||

items.text:
भ्रममाणौ तु तौ दृष्ट्वा रजकं रङ्गकारकम् ।
अयाचेतां सुरूपाणि वासांसि रुचिराननौ ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
bhramamāṇau tu tau dṛṣṭvā rajakaṃ raṅgakārakam |
ayācetāṃ surūpāṇi vāsāṃsi rucirānanau || 14 ||

items.text:
कंसस्य रजकः सोऽथ प्रसादारूढ़विस्मयः ।
बहून्याक्षेपवाक्यानि प्राहोच्चै राम-केशवौ ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
kaṃsasya rajakaḥ so'tha prasādārūṛhavismayaḥ |
bahūnyākṣepavākyāni prāhoccai rāma-keśavau || 15 ||

items.text:
ततस्तलप्रहारेण कृष्णस्तस्य दुरात्मनः ।
पातयामास कापेन रजकस्य शिरो भुवि ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
tatastalaprahāreṇa kṛṣṇastasya durātmanaḥ |
pātayāmāsa kāpena rajakasya śiro bhuvi || 16 ||

items.text:
हत्वादाय च वस्त्राणि पीतनीलाम्बरौ ततः ।
कृष्ण-रामौ मुदा युक्तौ मालाकारगृहं गतौ ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
hatvādāya ca vastrāṇi pītanīlāmbarau tataḥ |
kṛṣṇa-rāmau mudā yuktau mālākāragṛhaṃ gatau || 17 ||

items.text:
विकाशिनेत्रयुगलौ मालाकारोऽतिविस्मितः ।
एतौ कस्य कुतो वैतौ मैत्रेयाचिन्तयत् तदा ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
vikāśinetrayugalau mālākāro'tivismitaḥ |
etau kasya kuto vaitau maitreyācintayat tadā || 18 ||

items.text:
पीतनीलाम्बरधरौ तौ दृष्ट्वातिमनोहरौ ।
स तर्कयामास तदा भुवं देवावुपागतौ ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
pītanīlāmbaradharau tau dṛṣṭvātimanoharau |
sa tarkayāmāsa tadā bhuvaṃ devāvupāgatau || 19 ||

items.text:
विकाशिमुखपद्माभ्यां ताभ्यां पुष्पाणि याचितः ।
भुवं विष्टभ्य हस्ताभ्यां पस्पर्श शिरसा महीम् ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
vikāśimukhapadmābhyāṃ tābhyāṃ puṣpāṇi yācitaḥ |
bhuvaṃ viṣṭabhya hastābhyāṃ pasparśa śirasā mahīm || 20 ||

items.text:
प्रसादपरमौ नाथौ मम गेहमुपागतौ ।
धन्योऽहमर्ज्जयिष्यामीत्याह तौ माल्यजीवकः ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
prasādaparamau nāthau mama gehamupāgatau |
dhanyo'hamarjjayiṣyāmītyāha tau mālyajīvakaḥ || 21 ||

items.text:
ततः प्रह्टश्टवदनस्तयोः पुष्पाणि कामतः ।
चारूण्येतान्यथैतानि प्रददौ स विलोभयन ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ prahṭaśṭavadanastayoḥ puṣpāṇi kāmataḥ |
cārūṇyetānyathaitāni pradadau sa vilobhayana || 22 ||

items.text:
पुनः पुनः प्रणम्यासौ मालाकारौ नरोत्तमौ ।
ददौ पुष्पाणि चारूणि गन्धवन्त्यमलानि च ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
punaḥ punaḥ praṇamyāsau mālākārau narottamau |
dadau puṣpāṇi cārūṇi gandhavantyamalāni ca || 23 ||

items.text:
मालाकाराय कृष्णोऽपि प्रसन्नः प्रददौ वरान ।
श्रीस्त्वां मतूसंश्रया भद्र! न कदाचित् प्रहास्तयि ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
mālākārāya kṛṣṇo'pi prasannaḥ pradadau varāna |
śrīstvāṃ matūsaṃśrayā bhadra! na kadācit prahāstayi || 24 ||

items.text:
बलहानिर्न ते सौम्य! धनहानिस्थथैव च ।
यावद्दिनानि तावज्व न नशिष्यति सन्ततिः ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
balahānirna te saumya! dhanahānisthathaiva ca |
yāvaddināni tāvajva na naśiṣyati santatiḥ || 25 ||

items.text:
बुक्त्वा च विपुलान् भोगांस्तमन्ते मतूप्रसादजम् ।
ममानुस्मरणां प्राप्य दिव्यं लोकमवाप्स्यसि ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
buktvā ca vipulān bhogāṃstamante matūprasādajam |
mamānusmaraṇāṃ prāpya divyaṃ lokamavāpsyasi || 26 ||

items.text:
धर्म्मे मनश्व ते भद्र!सर्व्वकालं भविष्यति ।
युष्मत्सन्ततिजातानां दीर्घमायुर्भविष्यति ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
dharmme manaśva te bhadra!sarvvakālaṃ bhaviṣyati |
yuṣmatsantatijātānāṃ dīrghamāyurbhaviṣyati || 27 ||

items.text:
नोपसर्गादिकं दोषं युष्मत्सन्ततिसम्भवः ।
सम्प्राप्स्यति महाभाग!यावत् सूर्य्यो धरिष्यति ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
nopasargādikaṃ doṣaṃ yuṣmatsantatisambhavaḥ |
samprāpsyati mahābhāga!yāvat sūryyo dhariṣyati || 28 ||

items.text:
इतुक्त्वा तदूगृहात् कृष्णो बलदेवसहायवान् ।
निर्ज्जगाम मुनिश्वेष्ठ! मालाकारेण पूजितः ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr:
ituktvā tadūgṛhāt kṛṣṇo baladevasahāyavān |
nirjjagāma muniśveṣṭha! mālākāreṇa pūjitaḥ || 29 ||

en_chapter: Parāçara said:—Having thus praised Vishnu, standing in the stream that descendant of the Yadu race worshipped the lord of all with flowers, incense and all other beautiful articles. Having withdrawn his mind from every thing else and devoted it to Vishnu, he engaged, for some time, in the meditation, "I am Brahman" and then desisted from his abstraction. Then considering himself as blessed, the high-minded Akrura got up from the waters of the Yamuna and came to the chariot. Like before, he again saw stationed on the car Rāma and Krishna. Seeing Akrura thus amazed, Krishna said—"Forsooth, O Akrura, your eyes are expanded with surprise. Methinks you have seen something wonderful in the waters of the Yamuna".

Akruka said:—"O Achyuta, the wonder I saw in the waters, I behold here, before me in a bodily shape; I am united with thee, Krishna, the marvel I have seen and whose wonderous form is the universe. No more of this, let us go to Mathura, O Slayer of Madhu—I am afraid of Kansa. Oh! fie on them who eat the bread of another". Saying this he urged on the quick steeds and they arrived after sunset, at Mathura, When they came in sight of the city, Akrura said to Krishna and Rāma "You must now go on foot, whilst I proceed alone in the car; and you must not go to the house of Vasudeva for the elder has been banished by Kansa on your account".

Parāçara said:—Having said this Akrura alone entered the city of Mathura, Rāma and Krishna proceeded thereto following the public road. All the females and males of Mathura espied the two brothers with delight. And they went along sportively looking like two young elephants. As they roamed about, they saw a washerman colouring clothes and, with smiling countenances, they went and wanted of him some of his fine linen. He was a washerman of Kansa and was made insolent by his master's favour, so he remonstrated hard with Rāma and Kesava. Thereupon Krishna, in rage, struck down the head of that vicious-souled (washerman) on earth. Having thus killed him and taken yellow and blue raiment Krishna and Rāma, delightedly came to a flower-seller's shop. Seeing them, having expansive eyes, the flower-seller was astonished and thought, O Maitreya, who could they be or whence could they have come. Beholding two youths so lovely, dressed in yellow and blue garments, he took them to be divinities descended upon earth. Being asked for some flowers, by them, having mouths budding like lotuses he placed his hands upon the ground and touched it with his head, saying—"My lords have shown me great kindness, by coming to my house, fortunate that I am; I will pay them homage". Having said this, the flower-seller, with a smiling face, gave them whatever choice flowers they selected, to gain their favour. Prostrating himself again and again before them, he presented them again and again with flowers beautiful, fragrant and fresh. Being much pleased with him, Krishna gave him the blessing—"Fortune, O good friend, who depends on me, shall never forsake thee. Thou shalt never lose strength or wealth and thy family shall never be extinct. Enjoying many things, thou shalt, in the end, remembering me, attain to the region of the celestials. O good friend, thy mind shall always be in virtue and those, who shall be born in thy race, shall be long-lived. O great one, as long as the sun shall exist, none, in thy race, shall be disturbed with famine or other troubles".
Parāçara said:—Having said this and been worshipped by the flower-seller, O foremost of Munis, Krishna in the company of Balarāma, issued out of his house.
